mechanism_narrative: A 2% quarterly increase in Real GDP (GDPC1) indicates strengthening economic growth, leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of quarters with 2%+ GDPC1 growth, or walk-forward Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5%, signaling a tightening monetary cycle, S&P 500 forward returns are likely to be negative over the next 20 trading days due to increased borrowing costs.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2.5%, or walk-forward Rank IC < 0.01 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Joint behavior of rising PAYEMS (non-farm employment) and falling UNRATE (unemployment rate) over 3 months indicates a strong labor market, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 1% & UNRATE falls > 0.2pp in 3 months
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.04 over any 1.5-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in strong labor market periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 5% monthly increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) signals increased economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 45% of months with 5%+ INDPRO growth, or walk-forward Rank IC < 0.025 over any 2.5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) growth exceeds 8% over 6 months, indicating strong consumer spending, S&P 500 forward returns are likely to be positive over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances with 8%+ RSAFS growth, or walk-forward Rank IC < 0.015 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Joint behavior of FEDFUNDS below 1.5% and CPIAUCSL (inflation rate) below 2% over 2 months indicates an accommodative monetary environment, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in accommodative periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5% monthly decrease in UNRATE (unemployment rate) signals improving labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of months with 0.5%+ UNRATE decrease, or walk-forward Rank IC < 0.02 over any 1.5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (housing starts) growth exceeds 15% over 3 months, indicating strong housing market activity, S&P 500 forward returns are likely to be positive over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 45% of instances with 15%+ HOUST growth, or walk-forward Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.
